subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: China's Surveillance State
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: China's Surveillance State.

hook.text: In Xinjiang, cameras scan faces, phones are searched at checkpoints, and an app tracks every movement.

buildup.text: China operates the world's most extensive surveillance network: over 600 million cameras and growing.

discovery.text: The social credit system links surveillance data to rewards and punishments — from travel bans to loan denials.

twist.text: China exports its surveillance technology to over 80 countries, spreading its model of digital authoritarianism.

climax.text: China shows what happens when surveillance has no democratic checks: total control of a population's behavior.

punchline.text: Total surveillance. Zero accountability. Exported globally.

quiz.question: How many countries has China exported its surveillance technology to?
options: None — it's restricted to domestic use
